At the start, established by Picture 1, the East Asian man in his early thirties with light stubble, speaking Mandarin at a normal, slightly quick pace with no dead air (S2) sits across the small wooden table from the East Asian young woman in her late twenties (S1) by the rain-streaked tavern window at night, both under bright warm-white light. He holds the plain unlabeled white ceramic bottle — a cylindrical straight body with a flat shoulder and short neck, its red cap topped with a thin gold ring, the whole bottle glossy plain white with no text, letters, logo, label or print, its shape matching the supplied bottle reference exactly — already tilted and pouring into one of the two clear glass stemmed cups on the table; its red cap sits removed and set separately at the side of the table with the bottle mouth open, and at no point in the shot does he twist, unscrew, or press the cap back onto the bottle. She stares at the bottle, caught off guard, going still. The camera holds a steady handheld shot at eye level as he finishes filling that cup, then tilts the bottle to fill the second clear glass stemmed cup to the same level, both pours landing cleanly inside the stemmed bowls with no spill. He slides one filled cup a short distance across the wood until it rests directly in front of her, then lifts the bottle upright and sets it back down on the table, the red cap still left separately at the side, never recapped. Speaking low and steady, weighting five years of restraint into every word, he says: <d>[Chinese]你送的。我留了五年。</d> He pauses briefly, then continues in the same low voice: <d>[Chinese]一人问一个。问的人，喝一杯。</d> She keeps staring at the bottle and the two filled cups, saying nothing, her composure held together only by effort. By the end of the shot, the two filled cups, the cup pushed in front of her, the upright bottle, and the separately placed red cap settle into the exact positions and composition established by Picture 2.
